ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure gives the broken-line graph of y = f'(x). It can be seen that from x=0 to x=2, f'(x)=3, and it is a horizontal line; the point (2,3) is marked. After that, the broken line descends, passes through the x-axis at x=4, and reaches the marked point (5,-1). Then the broken line rises, and returns to y=0 when x=6. Then reason: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, f(6)=f(0)+∫_0^6 f'(x) dx. Calculate the signed area between the graph and the x-axis: on [0,2] it is a rectangle, with area 2·3=6; on [2,4] it is a triangle above the x-axis, with area (1/2)·2·3=3; on [4,5] it is a triangle below the x-axis, with area -(1/2)·1·1=-0.5; on [5,6] it is a triangle below the x-axis, with area -(1/2)·1·1=-0.5. Therefore the net amount of change is 6+3-0.5-0.5=8. Given f(0)=7, so f(6)=7+8=15.
